notes: Reading B, from the text. §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.1 lists library-names (7) and text-names (15) among the disjoint sets "Within a given source program", and every user-defined word "can belong to one and only one" of them; listing the two sets has content only for the source program as written, since after COPY processing no text-name or library-name remains to be disjoint from anything. XII.2.4 GR1 states the ORDER of compilation ("logically equivalent to processing all COPY statements prior to"), not that the words of a COPY statement are not words of the source program. The next edition confirms it: ISO 2002 Annex F.2 item 135, a substantive change, says text-names and library-names "are now system-names, instead of user-defined words, and do not have to be different from user-defined words" - which they did have to be in 1985. So an index-name spelled as a COPY text-name or library-name of the same source program violates SR14 / the disjoint sets and must be refused at --std 85; the compiler accepts it (u-copy: COPY IX beside INDEXED BY IX; own u-lib: COPY TX OF LIBX beside INDEXED BY LIBX) and runs. The rest of SR14 conforms (the read's and the refuter's probes: a repeated index-name COBOL6863; IX also a data-, paragraph-, section-, condition-, file-, mnemonic-, alphabet-, program-, class-, symbolic-character, cd- or report-name COBOL2692). Sibling (not this row): the same hole applies to every user-defined word kind, e.g. own probe u-dn, a data-name TX beside COPY TX, also compiles; that is the disjoint-set rule of §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.1 and the fix belongs in the one word-type funnel (CheckOneTypePerWord), fed with the text-names and library-names the preprocessor resolved, gated to 1985. PARTIAL, accepts illegal source. kb/Work PB5482 holds the defect (adjudication: held-85/set8/decisions.json (the adjudication of coderead-85/held-9.json, the 1985 read 4)).

next.reason: 1985 requires 'Index-name-1 must be a unique word within the program'. 1985 qualification (§1985:IV.4.3.8.1) has no format that qualifies an index-name, so a duplicate index-name is refused. 2023 adds Format 3 qualified-index-name to 8.4.2.2.2. §2023:8.4.2.2.3 SR6 says 'The qualification of an index-name may include the name of the table with which the index-name is associated'. §2023:8.4.2.2.3 SR1 requires uniqueness only 'For each non unique user-defined name that is explicitly referenced ... through a sequence of qualifiers'. Two tables may now share an index-name: refused in 1985, accepted in 2023 when every reference is qualified.
